title: Adab of sleep
hook: the one thing no one can do on purpose, and the remembrance that goes with it

segments.voice: Yesterday, the adab of travel, and your line: travel remembering. Did a trip begin or end with a line? Today, the shortest journey of every day: the one into sleep. Day one thousand two hundred ninety-seven.

Lights off. Phone face down. And then the one thing in the day nobody can do on purpose: fall asleep. You can't push your way into it. You can only lie down and let go. The Qur'an treats that letting go as no small thing. In surah al-Zumar, in Pickthall's translation: "Allah receiveth (men's) souls at the time of their death, and that (soul) which dieth not (yet) in its sleep." Every night, something is handed over. Today: the manners of handing it over well.
screen: `LIGHTS OFF.` → `NOBODY FALLS ASLEEP ON PURPOSE.` → `EVERY NIGHT, A HANDING OVER.`

segments.voice: Start with al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, in Sahih al-Bukhari. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, told him, in paraphrase: when you go to your bed, make wudu as you would for prayer, then lie down on your right side, and say a short du'a handing yourself over to Allah. Make it your last words, he said. If you die that night, you die on the fitrah, the natural state. So the body is washed, as for prayer. It lies down a particular way. And the last words of the day are chosen, not left to whatever was on the screen. Then 'A'ishah adds something she saw night after night. Also in Bukhari, in paraphrase: when he went to bed, he cupped his hands together, blew into them lightly, and recited the three short surahs at the end of the Qur'an: al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas, the three quls, each beginning with the word qul, say. Then he wiped his hands over as much of his body as he could, starting with his head and face. And he did that three times. Last, two short sentences from Hudhayfah, in Bukhari. Lying down, he would say: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. Waking, he would say, in paraphrase: praise to Allah, who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the rising. Sleep called a small dying. Waking called a small rising. It's the verse from al-Zumar, folded into two lines a person can say in the dark. The adab of sleep isn't about the mattress. It's about what you hand over, and how.
screen: `WUDU, THEN THE RIGHT SIDE.` · `LAST WORDS, CHOSEN.` · `THREE QULS INTO CUPPED HANDS.` · `IN YOUR NAME I DIE AND I LIVE.`

segments.voice: The practice: sleep this way tonight. For now, just rehearse it. Settle, and breathe. See tonight: water on your hands and face, either wudu or simply washing. Lying down on your right side. If you know al-Ikhlas, say it slowly in your mind now: qul huwa Allahu ahad. If you pray, you can plan for your last words to be bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya, in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. If you don't, choose one thing from today to set down before you sleep, and see yourself setting it down. The bell holds the time.
Adab of sleep. The manners of lying down: wudu, the right side, the three quls, and a last word of remembrance before the day lets go. Today's word.

Your line: sleep with remembrance. Tonight, try one piece of it: wash first, lie on your right side, or let a remembrance be your last word. Tomorrow, the adab of knowledge. Day one thousand two hundred ninety-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims follow the Prophet's bedtime practice: making wudu, lying on the right side, reciting al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas into cupped hands and wiping over the body, and saying "bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya" before sleep.

praise to Allah, who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the rising.

fork.setup: al-Bara' has made wudu and lain down on his right side. the Prophet tells him what his last words of the night should be. what are they?
options: a short du'a handing himself over to Allah.
fork.reveal: make it your last words, the Prophet said: if you die that night, you die on the fitrah.

trapdoor: what you thought: the adab of sleep is a bedtime routine.
what it means: going to sleep as a small handing over: wudu, the right side, the three quls, and a last word of remembrance.
what a scholar hears: 'in Your name I die and I live' (Bukhari 6312) beside al-Zumar 39:42: the soul taken in sleep and returned on waking.
